Liam is now Adwarp, the open-source ad agent for LinkedIn Ads and Google Ads. This is its first release on npm and in the official MCP Registry.

### Install

- `npx -y adwarp --help` runs the CLI without installing anything.
- `claude mcp add adwarp -- npx -y adwarp mcp` registers the local MCP server with Claude Code. Other MCP clients run `npx` with the arguments `-y adwarp mcp`.
- `npm install -g adwarp` installs the `adwarp`, `adwarp-mcp` and `liam` commands.
- The Dockerfile at the root of the repo builds an image that runs the MCP server on stdio.

### What changed

- Commands, the MCP server name, setup prompts and links now say Adwarp. `liam` keeps working as an alias.
- Your setup carries over unchanged: the `~/.liads` folder, the `LIADS_*` variables and the `X-Liads-*` headers.
- The hosted endpoint is `https://mcp.adwarp.dev/api/mcp`. `https://liam-mcp.vercel.app/api/mcp` keeps working.
- The docs live as Markdown in `docs/`, and `docs/tools.json` lists all 35 tools and which ones the hosted endpoint serves.
- Adwarp is listed in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.adwarp-dev/adwarp`, with the npm package and the hosted endpoint.

Everything Adwarp creates on LinkedIn starts as a draft and goes live only when you explicitly ask. Google Ads campaigns are created paused and can only be switched on in Google Ads.
